comparison: Both strongly support the experimental design and methodology (C1, C21-C24, C32-C33, C110, C116-C118). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge successful demonstration of the one-pot scRNA-seq method. Peer review also includes HMM claims (C34-C35) in this evaluation, while OpenEval separates them into R2.

Both support the HMM genotype inference methodology (C48-C53). OpenEval provides quantitative validation of improvements (R² increase from 0.59 to 0.73, strain recovery increase to 65.7%). Peer reviewers accept the approach without raising concerns, treating it as a successfully addressed technical challenge.

Both support the DISCERN imputation approach (C44-C47, C72). OpenEval notes moderate R²=50.0% as appropriate caution against over-imputation while demonstrating utility. Peer reviewers accept the imputation as part of the rigorous method without challenging its effectiveness.

Both support validation against bulk sequencing (C55-C61). OpenEval provides detailed statistical evidence (comparable heritability, QTL numbers, non-significant effect size differences, high model similarity). Peer reviewers accept this validation without criticism, with Reviewer 2 explicitly appreciating the comparison.

Both support expression heritability findings (C64-C67, C76-C78, C101). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and internal consistency. Peer reviewers accept these findings as confirmatory evidence supporting the method's validity without raising concerns.

Both address variance partitioning (C26-C27, C68-C70, C73, C108-C109), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval finds the analysis comprehensive and internally consistent (SUPPORTED). Peer Reviewer 2 acknowledges it as novel but raises concerns about lack of statistical controls/error estimates and limited broader impact (UNCERTAIN).

Both support increased eQTL detection power (C79-C80, C82-C85). OpenEval emphasizes the 4-fold increase and linear relationship with sample size (R²=0.95). Peer reviewers accept this as a key benefit, with the editor noting 'several new biological insights' and Reviewer 1 acknowledging dramatically increased statistical power. Peer review includes C29 here while OpenEval places it in R11.

Both address regulatory hotspot correlations (C86-C92), but with different confidence. OpenEval finds the correlation statistically significant with mechanistic support and independent validation (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept general findings but note a critical limitation: the analysis uses external fitness data from previous work rather than single-cell fitness estimates (UNCERTAIN).

Both support cis vs. trans regulation findings (C4, C94-C97, C104-C105). OpenEval emphasizes the 2× higher odds for trans-eQTL affecting fitness (p=0.01). Peer reviewers accept these findings, with the editor highlighting trans-regulation's larger aggregate effect as a key contribution.

Both support the comparative advantage over bulk methods (C98-C100). OpenEval emphasizes the contrasting statistical results (non-significant in bulk vs. 2× higher odds in scRNA-seq). Peer reviewers implicitly accept this, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging the method doesn't require normalization for culture-to-culture variation.

Both support the overall achievement claims (C3, C29, C103 in OpenEval; C2-C3, C25, C102 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes recapitulation plus new discoveries. Peer reviewers describe it as a 'useful study' with 'several new biological insights,' confirming authors 'successfully demonstrated their stated goal.'

OpenEval supports the motivation and limitations of existing approaches (C5-C7, C17-C20) as appropriately cited general knowledge claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these contextual claims are implicitly accepted as part of the overall study framing.

OpenEval supports the historical and scientific context (C8-C16) as well-cited prior work establishing the scientific debate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this background is implicitly accepted as appropriate framing.

OpenEval supports the reference panel and experimental context claims (C30-C31, C111-C112, C114-C115) as appropriately cited factual descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological context claims.

OpenEval supports the missing heritability and epistasis discussion (C75, C107-C108) as consistent with variance partitioning results. Peer review R5 includes C108 but focuses on variance partitioning methodology concerns rather than epistasis interpretation.
OpenEval supports the comparative context from human studies (C106) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this cross-species comparison claim.

OpenEval supports the analytical approach and methodological distinctions (C2, C25, C28). While peer review R11 includes C2 and C25, it focuses on overall achievement rather than methodological differences. C28 (distinction from prior work) has no peer review evaluation.
